references.text: Moses commands the Israelites to build an altar of stones on Mount Ebal, specifying that they must not use iron tools on the stones—the same principle regarding unworked stones for building altars.
Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal from whole stones that were not shaped with iron tools, in accordance with the Lord's command in the Book of Moses.

During the construction of Solomon's temple, stones were used that had been fully prepared at the quarry, so that no sound of hammer, axe, or any iron tool was heard in the house during its building—an echo of the principle to avoid iron tools in sacred structures.
The preceding verses describing the altar's function and that it should be made of earth provide context for why unworked stones are an alternative.
An extension of the command to build an altar of stones, where the words of the law are to be written clearly on the stones—showing the stone altar as a testimony.
Deuteronomy 27:5 confirms and repeats the law from Exodus regarding building an altar of uncut stones without iron tools.
